name: Jasmine Crockett
contest: Texas U.S. Senate 2026 — Democratic Primary, March 3, 2026

biography.birthPlace: St. Louis, Missouri (grew up in Texarkana, Texas)
priorRoles: Texas State Representative, House District 100, 87th Legislature (January 2021–January 2023)
Founder, Crockett Law PLLC — civil rights, criminal defense, personal injury (2010–2022)
biography.education: B.A. Business Administration, Rhodes College (2003); J.D., University of Houston Law Center (2006). First African American UH Law Center graduate elected to U.S. House (in school's 75-year history at time of election).
biography.background: Civil rights attorney; represented 5,000+ Texans in court; represented BLM protesters pro bono in Dallas; public defender background. Member Congressional Progressive Caucus. House committee assignments: Judiciary (Ranking Member, Subcommittee on Oversight); Agriculture; Oversight and Accountability; Transportation and Infrastructure. Nationally known for combative media presence in House hearings.
biography.notes: Crockett publicly distances herself from the 'progressive' label in the 2026 Senate campaign, framing positions as 'common sense.' Campaign is strategically oriented toward Democratic base turnout expansion, not Republican/independent persuasion.

campaignWebsite.structuralNote: Senate campaign site lacked a consolidated platform page at launch (noted February 2026 by Dallas Express / Townhall). Issue sub-pages exist at /issues, /affordability, /healthcare-you-need-when-you-need-it, /workers-rights, /community-safety, and an energy/climate sub-page. Direct web fetch unavailable; positions reconstructed from search engine snippets of sub-pages and news coverage of site content.

statedPositions.detail: Campaign healthcare sub-page: calls for eliminating premiums, deductibles, copays; uncoupling healthcare from employment; covering dental, vision, mental health, reproductive care, prescription drugs. Explicit Medicare for All framing. Also states Medicaid expansion in holdout states (including Texas) is an immediate priority.
statedPositions.notes: Corroborated by M4A cosponsorship (Tier 1) and multiple debate reaffirmations (Tier 2). Two-track: M4A as long-term goal, Medicaid expansion + ACA subsidies as immediate deliverables.

statedPositions.quote: Americans pay 70% more because of Big Insurance companies with rising premiums and declining coverage
statedPositions.detail: Campaign healthcare page. Praised Biden's IRA drug price negotiation as progress. M4A cosponsorship implies government price-setting as the ultimate mechanism. Cited as Ranking Member of Judiciary Subcommittee on Oversight at a joint subcommittee hearing on skyrocketing health care costs.
statedPositions.notes: Government price-setting is implicit in M4A; also explicitly defends IRA drug price negotiation (which is a targeted negotiation, not full rate-setting).

statedPositions.quote: fight for people to have their basic needs met, to ensure one person, one job is enough to live with dignity and retire with security
statedPositions.detail: Campaign announcement framing (February 2026). AFL-CIO 100% + SEIU endorsement confirm safety net vote alignment. Supports Medicaid expansion, ACA subsidies, and earned income programs. Anti-tariff framing (roll back tariffs Day 1) is a safety net / affordability signal.
statedPositions.notes: Multiple corroborating sources. AFL-CIO 100% is Tier 1.

statedPositions.quote: [Progress has been made] from American Rescue Plan to Inflation Reduction Act
statedPositions.detail: Joined 153 House Democrats opposing Trump's pause of IRA and Bipartisan Infrastructure Law funding. Defends public investment in clean energy, infrastructure, and manufacturing. Supports PRO Act (ease union organizing). Opposes Trump tariffs as harmful but frames this as consumer/worker protection, not industrial policy rejection.
statedPositions.notes: Strong public investment orientation consistent with progressive Democratic baseline. Co-signed letter defending IRA funding disbursements (Tier 1 legislative action).

statedPositions.quote: we need to go back to the tax rates that were in place when Clinton was in office, and we were able to balance our budget while also being able to have people that have access to food, access to education, and access to healthcare
statedPositions.detail: AFL-CIO debate, January 24, 2026. Texas Tribune Q&A (February 4, 2026) adds: 'supports reinstating the previous corporate tax rate for large corporations.' Heritage Action 17% confirms consistent anti-tax-cut voting record.
statedPositions.notes: Clinton-era top rate was 39.6% (vs. current 37%). Corporate tax reversal of TCJA. Consistent with entire voting record. Tier 2 structured interview + Tier 1 Heritage Action corroboration.

statedPositions.quote: unlocking opportunities starts with a solid public school education... opportunities shouldn't be decided by zip code or tax bracket
statedPositions.detail: Campaign issues page and House.gov about page. Emphasizes safe schools, certified teachers, nurses, counselors, support staff. Note: In 118th Congress, she voted against a provision that would have excluded for-profit career schools from Pell Grant eligibility (distinct from K-12 voucher debate). No explicit statement found on Texas ESA vouchers or federal school choice programs.
statedPositions.notes: Insufficient direct evidence on K-12 vouchers. General public school orientation suggests Pole A, but cannot score with confidence. Scorer should consider omitting or scoring LOW.

statedPositions.quote: Most renters are paying well over 30% of their monthly income
statedPositions.detail: Introduced Combatting the Housing Supply Shortage Act: increases cap on Tax-Exempt Private Activity Bonds for multifamily housing construction in high-demand states (TX, CA). Also introduced Rural Housing Voucher Enhancement Act. Affordability sub-page on Senate website addresses housing, food, childcare.
statedPositions.notes: Bond incentive approach is market-incentivizing (not direct public housing or rent control). More moderate on affordability tools than her other positions. No rent control or housing-as-right language found.

statedPositions.quote: various housing supply must be created so that all residents can lead the life they want to live
statedPositions.detail: House.gov economy/jobs/housing page. Supply expansion is an explicit goal. Method is private bond financing incentive. No statement on exclusionary zoning, by-right approval, or federal preemption found.
statedPositions.notes: Supply goal is clear; mechanism is market-incentive (bonds). Position on zoning reform itself is unclear. Scorer should likely omit this axis or score LOW with heavy uncertainty.

statedPositions.quote: [Crockett] advocated for robust federal investment in public transportation infrastructure
statedPositions.detail: Member, House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee. Introduced transit worker safety amendment to FY2024 THUD Appropriations (included). Met with APTA leadership during 2025 Congressional Fly-In to advocate for transit funding. TX-30 district (Dallas) is transit-dependent.
statedPositions.notes: Pro-transit record is consistent but not emphatic — this is the most committee-work-driven signal, not ideological priority-signaling. Dallas district context supports this.

statedPositions.quote: I am a gun owner. I am licensed to carry. And I still believe we should ban assault weapons.
statedPositions.detail: AFL-CIO debate (January 24, 2026). Campaign community safety page: ban assault weapons and bump stocks, universal background checks on all gun sales, close loopholes that allow dangerous people to access guns, strengthen safe storage. Cosponsor of Assault Weapons Ban of 2025. Giffords describes her as 'one of the nation's foremost gun safety champions.'
statedPositions.notes: Multiple Tier 1 and Tier 2 sources. Gun owner framing is tactical in Texas context — positions remain firmly pro-regulation. Giffords endorsement is Tier 1 organizational scorecard signal.

statedPositions.quote: ending qualified immunity for police officers... demilitarizing the police by ending the transfer of military weapons to local police departments
statedPositions.detail: House.gov criminal justice page. Voted NO on House spending bill with expanded ICE funding. Introduced TRACK ICE Act (transparency in immigration enforcement flights). Civil rights attorney background; represented BLM protesters pro bono. Reacted strongly when DOJ ended police reform agreements (2025). Introduced policing reform legislation in TX House. Supports civilian oversight.
statedPositions.notes: Clear reform-focused, not defund/abolish. End qualified immunity + demilitarize = significant oversight/accountability position (score ~2-3 on axis). Multiple corroborating sources.

statedPositions.quote: applauded President Biden for commuting the sentences of 2,500 non-violent drug offenders
statedPositions.detail: Led clemency efforts for federal crack cocaine convictions. Introduced Democracy Restoration Act (July 2025) — would restore federal voting rights for all Americans released from incarceration. As TX State Rep (2021): passed legislation wiping in-court fees for recently incarcerated persons. Public defender background emphasizes rehabilitation over punishment.
statedPositions.notes: Strong rehabilitation and decarceration orientation across multiple sources and legislative actions. Consistent from state to federal level.

statedPositions.quote: Trump has no plan AT ALL to address the climate crisis. Texas is a leader in many renewable energies and I plan to end our reliance on fossil fuels and expand our clean and sustainable energy production
statedPositions.detail: House.gov energy and climate page. LCV 97% lifetime score; LCV endorsed 2022 and 2024; named in LCV 'Champions of Color.' Joined 153 House Democrats opposing Trump's pause of IRA clean energy funding. Co-founded Texas House Energy & Climate Caucus (state level, 2021). Spoke out against LNG export expansion.
statedPositions.notes: LCV 97% lifetime is Tier 1. Multiple Tier 2 sources corroborate. Campaign sub-page target: 100% renewable energy (year target varies by source — 2035 referenced in some reports). Clearly at or near Pole A.

statedPositions.quote: determined to lead the charge in electrification, and adoption of renewable fuels... plans to end our reliance on fossil fuels
statedPositions.detail: Eliminate fossil fuel subsidies; invest in green infrastructure in underserved communities; introduced Farm to Fuselage Act (bipartisan sustainable aviation fuel). Opposed LNG export expansion (spoke out against Biden administration's LNG project approvals that LCV tracked). Defended IRA clean energy provisions.
statedPositions.notes: Renewables-first, anti-fossil fuel framing is unambiguous. No all-of-the-above language. LCV 97% lifetime corroborates at Tier 1 level.

statedPositions.detail: No specific statement found on environmental review timelines, permitting reform, or expedited project approval. LCV 97% suggests she would not support weakening environmental review, but no direct evidence of strengthening precautionary review either.
statedPositions.notes: Omit this axis — no direct evidence. Scorer should not infer from LCV score alone.

statedPositions.quote: at the end of the day I think we need to clean house from top to bottom... ICE is a rogue organization
statedPositions.detail: AFL-CIO debate (January 24, 2026): said she would 'abolish ICE if given the chance.' Also characterized position as 'cleaning house' (overhaul), not strict abolition. NBC News separately reported she called for ICE overhaul. El Paso (Feb 22, 2026): 'border security and immigration are two separate things' — supports improved border technology, not more walls. Campaigned in Laredo (Feb 27, 2026): 'we believe in border security.' Voted NO on House spending bill with ICE funding expansion. Introduced TRACK ICE Act.
statedPositions.notes: Notable internal tension: 'abolish if given the chance' vs. 'clean house' vs. pro-border-security framing in border communities. Her House voting record (NO on ICE funding) is the Tier 1 signal. The overhaul framing is the most reliable description of her actual position — not strict abolition, not status quo. Tactical audience-calibration is evident.

evidenceSummary.overallConfidence: HIGH for 10 of 16 axes based on Tier 1 voting records and scorecards. MEDIUM for 2 axes (housing). No evidence for 4 axes (school choice, public health, permitting, zoning).
keyObservations: Crockett holds one of the most consistently progressive voting records in the House Democratic caucus as measured by multiple independent third-party scorecards. Her positions on healthcare, climate, labor, firearms, criminal justice, and tax policy are all near Pole A.

Her housing approach is notably more moderate than her other positions. The Tax-Exempt Bond legislation is a market-incentivizing tool, not direct public investment or rent control — this is consistent with Texas political context but represents a genuine moderate lean on housing tools.
The ICE 'abolish vs. overhaul' framing shows strategic audience-calibration. The Tier 1 signal (No on ICE funding, TRACK ICE Act) points to accountability/overhaul orientation.

The PCCC-over-Crockett endorsement of Talarico (despite Crockett's higher AFL-CIO scores) reflects a tension between legislative performance and economic policy leadership/positioning that the scorer should note but not over-weight.

No evidence of departure from progressive consensus on any scored axis across the full House record. The Heritage Action 17% + AFL-CIO 100% combination places her firmly in the top-quintile of progressive House members.
evidenceSummary.scorerGuidance: Score axes with HIGH and MEDIUM confidence; omit axes explicitly flagged as missing. Do not interpolate housing_supply_zoning from housing_affordability_tools — these are distinct positions and the evidence only supports the latter. The econ_school_choice omission is intentional — progressive default is inferable from background but should not be scored without direct evidence per methodology.
